 Derrick White notched 16 points (6-of-11 FGs), four rebounds, two assists and two steals over 23 minutes in Sunday’s win over the Mavericks.
 White has been hot-and-cold from three-point range throughout his Celtics tenure, but he was locked-in during this contest, knocking down 4-of-9 from downtown. He didn’t end up with a block, but did come away with a pair of thefts as he was able to sit out nearly the entire second half as Boston built a massive lead, enabling them to cruise to the finish line. The Celtics have a four-game week on tap that includes showdowns against the Magic, Nuggets, Clippers and Warriors.

 Derrick White had 19 points (7-of-15 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), a rebound, seven assists, a steal, four blocks and three 3-pointers in the win over the Raptors. 
 One of the big reasons why you have Derrick White on your fantasy team is for the blocks, and he got you four of them today. White hasn’t exactly been what you would want from the scoring department this season, but its hard to complain about this performance. White is 32 years old, so the decline is relatively expected. 
 Derrick White 
 BOS 
 Guard 
 #9 
 Derrick White amassed 18 points (6-of-10 FGs, 2-of-3 FTs), four rebounds, five assists and one steal over 25 minutes in a lopsided win over the Hornets on Friday. 
 White enjoyed his best shooting performance from beyond the arc in some time, connecting on 4-of-6 attempts after shooting just 29 percent from three-point range through his first eight games. He would’ve notched his second consecutive 20-point effort, but he was able to sit out most of the second half with Boston leading by nearly 40 points. The Celtics close out a four-game week with a road matchup against the Bucks, who White torched for a season-high 24 points earlier this week.

 Derrick White amassed 24 points (7-of-18 FGs, 9-of-9 FTs), four rebounds, seven assists, one steal, two blocks and one three-pointer in Wednesday’s win over the Bucks. 
 White has gotten off to a slow start, as he began Wednesday averaging 11.1 points per game. With Jayson Tatum out, the Celtics guard had more room to attack offensively, and he took advantage. White shot 1-of-7 from beyond the arc, which hurt his overall field-goal percentage, but he finished with a season-high point total and a complete stat line. The “buy low” window may have closed with this performance.

 Derrick White tallied 12 points (4-of-8 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), two rebounds, two assists, two steals and two three-pointers in Sunday’s win over the Magic. 
 White took a back seat offensively on Sunday, but he did a little bit of everything to help the Celtics end their week with a victory. After shooting a career-worst 39.4 percent from the field last season, White is up to 47.4 percent through six games. His category-league value hasn’t reached his ADP yet, but fantasy managers shouldn’t worry.

 Derrick White tallied 17 points (6-of-9 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), three rebounds, two assists, four steals and one three-pointer in Wednesday’s exhibition against the Hornets. 
 White is coming off his worst season in field-goal percentage, making just 39.4 percent of his attempts. However, he still provided top-50 fantasy value because of everything else he does to help the Celtics win. Fantasy managers should expect White to bounce back with his shooting while still offering reliable fantasy value across the board. His ceiling may be somewhat limited, but his fantasy floor is strong and reliable.

 Guard 
 #9 
 Derrick White amassed 26 points (9-of-26 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), six rebounds, four assists, three blocks and five three-pointers in Saturday’s Game 7 loss to the 76ers. 
 White got his Game 7 off to an excellent start, scoring 19 points in the first half. However, the 76ers, specifically VJ Edgecombe, did a much better job of defending him in the second half. White made some history, joining Kevin Durant (2018) and Robert Covington (2020) as the only players to record at least five three-pointers and three blocks in a Game 7, but it wasn’t enough to get the shorthanded Celtics over the finish line. Shooting was an issue for the Celtics’ guard throughout the season, but the ability to fill a stat line preserved his fantasy value. Managers should expect more of the same from White in 2026-27, hopefully with a more accurate jump shot.

 Payton Pritchard tallied 32 points (12-of-21 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), four rebounds, five assists, one steal and six three-pointers in Sunday’s Game 4 win over the 76ers. 
 On a day when starter Derrick White (6/6/3/1/2 with two three-pointers) attempted just five shots, Pritchard stepped up with one of the best outings of his postseason career. The 32 points, a playoff career-high for Pritchard, were two shy of the Celtics franchise record for most in a playoff game by a reserve, which Kevin McHale still holds. While he made too many starts to qualify for NBA Sixth Man of the Year honors, Pritchard remains one of the best reserve scorers in the league. And he reminded Philadelphia of that in Game 4. The Celtics will look to close out the series on Tuesday night.

 Derrick White tallied 10 points (4-of-10 FGs, 0-of-1 FTs), three rebounds, six assists, one steal and two three-pointers in Sunday’s Game 1 win over the 76ers. 
 With six players in double figures and stars Jaylen Brown and Jayson Tatum combining to score 51 points, the Celtics did not need much scoring from White. Shooting 2-of-7 from three, the veteran guard dished out six assists and committed just one turnover. White’s ability to fill the stat line is what made him so valuable to fantasy managers during the regular season, and it has made him an important piece in Boston since his acquisition during the 2021-22 campaign.

 The Celtics have already ruled out four of their five starters for Sunday’s regular-season finale, as the outcome will not impact their playoff seeding. White’s absence should free up additional minutes for Ron Harper Jr. and Max Shulga. As for Queta, there will be more playing time available for Luka Garza, and Amari Williams could get rotation minutes as well.

 Jayson Tatum accumulated 32 points (11-of-18 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), seven rebounds, six assists and two steals over 30 minutes to lead the Celtics to a 131-94 blowout win over the Mavericks on Sunday.
 Tatum put together a feast-worthy stat line just in time for Thanksgiving, exploding for 21 third-quarter points to extend Boston’s lead to 33 and effectively put the game out of reach before the final period. It marked the 10th time he has scored at least 15 points in a quarter, the most in Celtics history since the play-by-play era began in 1996-97, just ahead of franchise legend Paul Pierce. He’s delivered second-round fantasy value, averaging 26.8 points, 6.1 rebounds, 7.3 assists, 0.6 steals and 0.8 blocks through 12 games this season. The Celtics have won six consecutive games and will kick off a busy four-game week against the Magic before heading out west to face the Nuggets, Clippers and Warriors.
 -  George Bissell

 Cooper Flagg tallied 17 points (5-of-15 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), three rebounds, four assists, one steal and one block over 27 minutes in Sunday’s loss to the Celtics.
 The Maine native did some real damage in the fourth quarter once the Celtics had already put the game away. It may have been garbage time, but it counts all the same for fantasy purposes. Simply put, Dallas looked like a completely different offense without primary initiator Kyrie Irving at point guard as he sat out the second night of a back-to-back in this one. The 19-year-old phenom has cooled off a bit over the last week, but he’s still averaging 23.5 points, 6.7 rebounds, 6.2 assists, 1.9 steals and 0.8 blocks through 13 games as one of the most impactful all-around contributors in fantasy. The Mavericks have a three-game week on tap that features showdowns against the Warriors, Clippers and Jazz.

 Zaccharie Risacher delivered 18 points (8-of-9 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs) and five rebounds over 27 minutes in Sunday’s blowout loss to the Celtics.
 Risacher was one of the few bright spots on an otherwise forgettable affair in Boston, as he saw huge minutes off the bench in a lopsided affair and was nearly perfect from the floor. His lone miss came from three-point range where he finished 1-of-2. The former top-overall pick from the 2024 NBA Draft fell out of favor in Atlanta, but he’s still young enough to envision a scenario where the change of scenery helps him turn things around. This effort certainly qualifies as a step in the right direction. The Mavericks have a three-game week coming up featuring contests against the Warriors, Clippers and Jazz.

 Shooting the ball efficiently was an issue for all Jazz starters except Mo Bamba, who went 10-of-13, so Peterson wasn’t alone in his struggles.  Mo Bamba accounted for 26 points (10-of-13 FGs, 0-of-3 FTs), five rebounds, four assists, two steals, one block and six three-pointers in Sunday’s loss to the Spurs.
 With Jaxson Hayes joining the list of injured Jazz big men, Bamba was inserted into the starting lineup on Sunday. He made the most of his opportunity, having one of the best games of his NBA career. Shockingly, Bamba went 6-of-6 from beyond the arc and recorded a full stat line. The Jazz play four games next week, starting with the Clippers on Tuesday. If they remain this shorthanded, Bamba’s worth a roll of the dice in deep leagues.
